title: Emerson Patriot radio
lede: Norman Bel Geddes’s Catalin table radio for Emerson: a grille of stacked horizontal bars beside a big round dial.
summary: A red Catalin case with a grille of cream horizontal bars and a large round dial. Norman Bel Geddes for Emerson, 1940.

source.label: Victoria and Albert Museum: Patriot Midget radio, W.31-1992

creator.name: Norman Bel Geddes (designer); Emerson Radio and Phonograph Corporation (manufacturer)

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected Daderot’s 2015 photograph of a Model 400 (FC-400) Patriot in the Museum für Angewandte Kunst Köln on [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Radio_Model_400_(FC-400)_Patriot,_Norman_Bel_Geddes,_Emerson,_Catalin_case_-_Museum_f%C3%BCr_Angewandte_Kunst_K%C3%B6ln_-_Cologne,_Germany_-_DSC09461.jpg) at 1920 px. Read the V&A record for W.31-1992 (blue case, red and white grille) through the V&A API. The two copies differ in color.

styles.note: Partial fit: the case is a rectangle, as the V&A notes, but the grille of stacked horizontal bars and the round dial are streamline signs.

context: The V&A says Bel Geddes (1893–1958) helped define streamline styling, but chose a rectilinear case for the Patriot, a “Stars and Stripes” design made in red, white, and blue combinations and linked to Emerson’s 25th anniversary; the knobs are embossed with stars. [V&A O85202](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O85202/patriot-midget-radio-bel-geddes-norman/).

The V&A copy has a blue case, a grille of alternating red and white bands, and two blue knobs; it measures 19 × 26.5 × 13.6 cm. [V&A O85202](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O85202/patriot-midget-radio-bel-geddes-norman/).
observed: The Cologne copy has a glossy red case with slightly rounded edges and a cream handle on top.
The left half of the front is a grille of seven cream bars stacked horizontally with dark gaps between them; the bars are flat on the front and slightly rounded at the ends.
The right half holds a large round dial with a cream ring of numbers and a red pointer; the small text on the dial reads “Emerson Radio and Phonograph Corp. N.Y. U.S.A.”
Two white knobs, each embossed with a five-pointed star, sit below the dial.
interpretation: The radio reduces the style to two signs: parallel horizontal bars and a circle. The bars read as speed lines even on a still box. The V&A’s caution matters: the case itself is not streamlined.
borrow: Pair a block of stacked horizontal bars with one large circle in a two-part layout.
Use red, cream, and navy as flat plastic colors with no gradient.

images.alt: Front view of a red plastic table radio in a museum case: a grille of seven cream horizontal bars on the left, a large round dial with a cream number ring on the right, two white star-embossed knobs, and a cream handle on top.

rights.statement: The photographer dedicated the photograph to the public domain (CC0), and notes that the radio is not subject to US copyright, only to a long-expired design patent. The radio is an American useful article. Norman Bel Geddes died in 1958.
